content.text: Identifiability requires informative excitation and an explicit candidate model. The experiment design must define excitation range, the steady operating point, measurement units, sampling clock, disturbance history and candidate model class. Parameter uncertainty should include instrument calibration, sensor drift, saturation, unmodeled modes, noise assumptions, and any prior engineering constraints. A fitted mean squared error is not a guarantee of correct uncertainty bounds, physical interpretation, robustness or ability to stabilize the actual machine. Domain context: 08_system_identification_and_uncertainty.md. A declared model is not a validated hardware controller.
uncertainty: No experimentally calibrated parameter uncertainty or sensor covariance verified
units: Model quantities and time units must be explicitly declared; scalar educational values are not measured

gaps: No experiment on actual controller, sensor, actuator or agent
